file_roles.evidence: 'opsLock.writeLock().lock()' in onDeActivate becomes 'opsLock.writeLock().lockInterruptibly()' inside a try that restores the flag and rethrows, 'Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); throw new IgniteInterruptedException(e)'. An uninterruptible acquire in a worker that shutdown must be able to interrupt is the wrong logic, and both ends of the deadlock are methods of this class.

rationale: The two dumps close the cycle. Main is inside 'IgniteServiceProcessor.stopProcessor(IgniteServiceProcessor.java:261)' and blocked joining the worker at 'GridWorker.join(GridWorker.java:242)', while the services-deployment-worker is parked on the write lock at 'IgniteServiceProcessor.onDeActivate(IgniteServiceProcessor.java:405)'. Shutdown holds what the worker waits for and waits for the worker, so making the worker's acquire interruptible is what breaks the cycle. Both frames name the gold file.
notes: The evidence is a JVM thread dump rather than anything the program logged, so no log site is recorded. It is still the most precise evidence seen so far: the dump names IgniteServiceProcessor.java:405, which is the exact line the fix changes.
